## What I checked

- **Repo state** — `~/onboard-test` is a brand-new git repo: branch `master`, zero commits, no remote, nothing tracked except `.claude/skills` and `.claude/rules` (both already symlinked to `~/test`, which is a full bassclef checkout).
- **Path A prerequisites** (standard GitHub-backed onboarding):
  - `claude` on PATH — yes
  - `gh` installed — **no** (`gh: command not found`)
  - GitHub remote configured — **no**
  - `.bassclef/init.manifest.json` present — no (so this isn't a "top-up" case either)

`gh` being completely absent (not just unauthenticated) means Path A can't run any of its GitHub steps — label creation, branch protection, environment setup all fail immediately.

## Where this stops

One more thing worth flagging regardless of which path: this repo is on `master` with no commits. Path A separately refuses to run from `main`/`master` (substrate scaffolding goes through a PR, not a direct commit) — so even with `gh` installed, you'd first need `git checkout -b chore/bassclef-bootstrap`.

**Which do you want?** `1` (local-only demo, no GitHub), `2` (I wait while you install/auth `gh`, then re-run), or `3` (stop here).
